blockers.title: The exact-pin lock still requires unresolved constraint and compatibility evaluation
blockers.detail: Changing resolutionInputs.request roots from {stableId, versionConstraint} to {stableId, version} does not make a multi-component closure producible. Every manifest dependency still has the shape {stableId, versionConstraint}, and lockSchema.resolved must be dependency-closed over those declarations. To decide that an exact-pinned dependency version satisfies its declaring edge, the resolver must evaluate the still-undefined versionConstraint language; if it ignores the constraint, the resulting set is not proven dependency-closed. The same fork exists for manifest compatibility declarations against resolutionInputs.hostCoreVersion/platform: admission checks them structurally only, so copying an admitted tuple either evaluates DR-111 windows during lock resolution or records an unverified compatibility selection. The subject therefore does exactly what the dispatch asks the reviewer to attack: its exact-pin form secretly evaluates windows/constraints or silently drops their meaning.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define a presently decidable exact-pin closure rule that accounts for every dependency edge and compatibility datum without interpreting DR-111-owned semantics, or keep lock production conditional on DR-111. Merely exact-pinning request roots is insufficient.

blockers.title: The repairLog is not a complete or mechanically resolvable account of the actual diff
blockers.detail: A duplicate-key-rejecting recursive v2-to-v3 comparison found 23 minimal changed paths. At least three changes are absent from the operations that purport to explain them: /date; /manifestSchema/fields/3/semantics (the new same-stableId sentence and changed collision scope); and /testCorpusRequirements/classes/0/requires/3 (the added 'lawful under collisionUniverse' text). The V2-A1 operation that intends to name the name-field type uses '/manifestSchema/fields name type', which is not a JSON Pointer and cannot resolve; the actual path is /manifestSchema/fields/3/type. The lock operation names the parent /testCorpusRequirements/classes/0/requires but describes only the exact-pin change at member 5, silently carrying the separate V2-A1 edit at member 3. META-v3 also omits the date change. Therefore basedOn.method's claim that every path not named by the v3 repairLog is unchanged is false.
blockers.requiredRepair: Make every v2-to-v3 edit explicit at resolving JSON-Pointer paths, including metadata and each independently motivated array-member/string edit; then repin the successor and repeat the independent diff.

shouldFix.title: The DIFFERENT-stableId qualifier is over-broad at the name-field site
shouldFix.detail: manifestSchema.fields[3].semantics now says a collision with a 'reserved root command of a DIFFERENT stableId' is refused, but reserved commands have no stableId. indexSchema.collisionUniverse also begins with the broad word 'Collisions', although reserved-list and within-manifest command-tree collisions are not cross-entry comparisons and remain unconditional under RJ-2. RJ-2 itself is still clear, so this is not an additional blocker, but the field and universe sentences should scope the carve-out explicitly to cross-entry live-name/alias/root comparisons and leave reserved/internal collisions unconditional.
